findings.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts guests array has no .max() bound and the mutation has no rate limiting, allowing an authenticated attendee to submit thousands of arbitrary email addresses that each receive an AttendeeScheduledEmail — an email amplification/spam vector

addGuests.handler.ts builds EventManager from the requesting user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's, so when a non-organizer adds a guest, updateCalendarAttendees runs against the wrong account and the third-party calendar/video event is never updated
addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 uses `&&` instead of `||` in isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)), denying team admins who are not owners

addGuests.handler.ts:47-48 passes a sentinel `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` for personal/dynamic bookings, running membership queries against a non-existent team instead of short-circuiting the permission check

addGuests.handler.ts:70-78 lowercases the blacklist but compares the incoming guest un-normalized (!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)), so a mixed-case address like Blocked@Example.com bypasses BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS

addGuests.handler.ts:76 duplicate detection uses exact string equality (guest === attendee.email), so a case variant like Bob@x.com is added alongside an existing bob@x.com, creating duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails

addGuests.schema.ts:5 omits the uniqueness refine that the client applies in AddGuestsDialog.tsx, so a direct tRPC call with a repeated email passes validation and createMany inserts two identical attendees

addGuests.handler.ts:74-95 duplicate check and the booking.update/createMany are not atomic and there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email), so two concurrent add-guest requests for the same address both insert

addGuests.handler.ts passes the raw `guests` input to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of `uniqueGuests`, causing email-manager.ts to misclassify a pre-existing attendee as new and send them an AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the 'guests added' notification

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:528-534 calendarEvent.team?.members loop can never execute for this flow because the evt built in addGuests.handler.ts never sets a `team` property, so team co-hosts receive no notification that guests were added

addGuests.handler.ts:26-44 does not check booking.status, allowing guests to be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED, or past bookings, which then triggers calendar updates and 'booking confirmed' emails for a dead event

addGuests.handler.ts eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) is not wrapped in try/catch, so a provider failure returns an error to the user after attendees were already committed to the DB, leaving silently-added guests and no emails

addGuests.handler.ts:58-61 prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) throws a raw Prisma NotFoundError as an unhandled 500 for bookings with a null userId instead of a typed TRPC error

No tests accompany the new handler — the authorization matrix (organizer/attendee/team admin/unrelated user), blacklist filter, duplicate filter, and the uniqueGuests.length === 0 path are all untested
addGuests.handler.ts catch block discards the error and uses console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") instead of the project logger, making email failures undiagnosable in production

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:41-42 builds `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` which is always truthy, making the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback dead code and showing users raw text like 'FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission'

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:66 onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog} bypasses the Cancel button's reset, so dismissing via Escape/overlay/X leaves multiEmailValue and isInvalidEmail populated and reopening shows stale emails and a stale error banner

packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:26 uses key={index} on a list that supports removal, so deleting a middle entry re-associates DOM/input state (focus, uncontrolled internals, validation) with the wrong row

packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:2 imports Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip from the @calcom/ui barrel while packages/ui/index.tsx exports the component via MultiEmailLazy, creating a barrel cycle that can yield undefined components depending on module resolution order

packages/ui/form/MultiEmailLazy.tsx:3 comment '/** These are like 40kb that not every user needs */' is copy-pasted from PhoneInputLazy/AddressInputLazy and is false — MultiEmail is a ~90-line component with no heavy dependency, so the stated lazy-loading rationale is wrong

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts guests array has no .max() bound and the mutation has no rate limiting, allowing an authenticated attendee to submit thousands of arbitrary email addresses that each receive an AttendeeScheduledEmail — an email amplification/spam vector

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()`/size bound in `addGuests.schema.ts`, and `addGuestsHandler` performs `createMany` for all `uniqueGuests` without any explicit cap. It then constructs `evt.attendees` from the updated booking and calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, where `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends an email per attendee (mapping over `calendarEvent.attendees`), meaning a caller can cause the system to send emails to a very large number of addresses in one request. The diff also shows no rate limiting/throttling around this authed procedure. This is a verifiable email amplification/spam vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts builds EventManager from the requesting user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's, so when a non-organizer adds a guest, updateCalendarAttendees runs against the wrong account and the third-party calendar/video event is never updated

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the handler explicitly allows non-organizers to proceed (isAttendee is checked and can grant access). However, it builds the EventManager using credentials from the requesting user: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is `ctx.user`. The booking organizer is fetched separately as `organizer` (based on `booking.userId`), but their credentials are never used. If an attendee (or team admin/owner who isn't the organizer) adds guests, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run using the requester's integrations/credentials rather than the organizer's, which is a concrete correctness defect for updating the organizer-owned external calendar event/video meeting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 uses `&&` instead of `||` in isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...)), denying team admins who are not owners
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same permission-check bug: using && requires a user to be both team admin and owner, and it should be || so either role grants access. It also notes the impact (admins denied if not owners).

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:47-48 passes a sentinel `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` for personal/dynamic bookings, running membership queries against a non-existent team instead of short-circuiting the permission check

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0` being passed into `isTeamAdmin`/`isTeamOwner`, so for bookings without a team it will still execute those queries with `teamId = 0` rather than skipping them. However, from the diff alone it’s not verifiable that this causes a bug/security issue (it likely just returns `false` and falls back to the organizer/attendee checks). The finding characterizes it as a permission-check problem, but the current logic still denies access unless the user is organizer/attendee, so the impact is at most an inefficiency unless external code (not shown) misbehaves on `teamId=0`.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same flaw: the blacklist is normalized to lowercase but the incoming guest email is not, so the includes() check can be bypassed with mixed/uppercase input, defeating BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:76 duplicate detection uses exact string equality (guest === attendee.email), so a case variant like Bob@x.com is added alongside an existing bob@x.com, creating duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees via `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`, which is a case-sensitive comparison with no normalization (e.g., `toLowerCase()`). Since incoming `guests` are not lowercased (schema only validates email format) and existing `attendee.email` may be stored in a different case, a case-variant like `Bob@x.com` can pass the filter even if `bob@x.com` already exists, resulting in a duplicate attendee row/email for the same logical address. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts:5 omits the uniqueness refine that the client applies in AddGuestsDialog.tsx, so a direct tRPC call with a repeated email passes validation and createMany inserts two identical attendees
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying bug: repeated/duplicate emails in the input are not deduplicated/validated for uniqueness server-side, so createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows when a client submits the same email multiple times.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:74-95 duplicate check and the booking.update/createMany are not atomic and there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email), so two concurrent add-guest requests for the same address both insert

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler reads the current attendees (booking.findFirst include attendees) and filters `guests` against that snapshot (lines ~74-95) before later doing a separate `prisma.booking.update({ attendees: { createMany: ... }})`. There is no transaction/locking and no `skipDuplicates`/upsert behavior, so two concurrent requests adding the same email can both pass the pre-check and then both attempt to insert. Whether this results in duplicate rows or a DB constraint error depends on a unique constraint that is not shown in this diff, but the non-atomic check+insert race is real in the introduced code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts passes the raw `guests` input to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of `uniqueGuests`, causing email-manager.ts to misclassify a pre-existing attendee as new and send them an AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the 'guests added' notification

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code filters input `guests` into `uniqueGuests` to exclude already-existing attendees and blacklisted emails, and only creates attendees for `uniqueGuests`. However it later calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (raw input), not `uniqueGuests`. In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses the passed `newGuests` list to decide per attendee: `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email))` it sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail`, else it sends `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. Therefore, if the user includes an email that is already an attendee (and at least one truly new guest so the handler proceeds), that existing attendee email remains in `guests` and will be treated as “new” by `sendAddGuestsEmails`, causing them to receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` instead of the guests-added notification. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/email-manager.ts:528-534 calendarEvent.team?.members loop can never execute for this flow because the evt built in addGuests.handler.ts never sets a `team` property, so team co-hosts receive no notification that guests were added

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In addGuests.handler.ts, the CalendarEvent `evt` passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is constructed without any `team` field (it sets title/type/organizer/attendees/etc., but no `team` or `team.members`). In email-manager.ts, `sendAddGuestsEmails` only notifies additional team recipients inside `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) { for (const teamMember of calendarEvent.team.members) ... }`. Given the `evt` built in this diff, `calendarEvent.team` will be undefined, so that loop cannot run and co-host/team members will not receive `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` notifications from this flow (only the base organizer email send occurs).

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:26-44 does not check booking.status, allowing guests to be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED, or past bookings, which then triggers calendar updates and 'booking confirmed' emails for a dead event

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the handler fetches the booking by id and then proceeds to update attendees (prisma.booking.update), call eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking), and sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with no check of any booking lifecycle state (e.g., booking.status) or whether the booking is in the past. The query does not filter by status/time either (where: { id: bookingId }). As a result, guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/past bookings if the caller passes the permission checks, and this will still trigger calendar attendee updates and emails. Additionally, sendAddGuestsEmails sends AttendeeScheduledEmail to emails in newGuests, which is effectively the “scheduled/confirmed” email path, supporting the finding’s impact description.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) is not wrapped in try/catch, so a provider failure returns an error to the user after attendees were already committed to the DB, leaving silently-added guests and no emails

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the code first commits new attendees to the DB via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` and only afterwards calls `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` with no try/catch or transaction. If `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (e.g., external calendar/provider failure), the mutation will error back to the client while the DB change has already been persisted, and the email-sending block won’t run. This creates a real partial-update/inconsistent-state risk introduced by the diff (even if it’s not strictly “silent” because the client would receive an error).

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:58-61 prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }) throws a raw Prisma NotFoundError as an unhandled 500 for bookings with a null userId instead of a typed TRPC error

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the organizer is fetched via prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } }). If booking.userId is null/undefined, this queries id=0 and will throw from Prisma (e.g., P2025 / NotFoundError). There is no try/catch converting that into a TRPCError, so the procedure would surface as an internal/untyped server error rather than a typed TRPC NOT_FOUND/BAD_REQUEST. The use of booking.userId || 0 elsewhere in the handler suggests userId may be nullable, making this a real failure mode introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests accompany the new handler — the authorization matrix (organizer/attendee/team admin/unrelated user), blacklist filter, duplicate filter, and the uniqueGuests.length === 0 path are all untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new functionality (TRPC handler, UI dialog, email templates) but does not add or modify any test files. However, “no tests accompany this change” is a process/coverage concern rather than a concrete, verifiable defect in the code introduced by the diff. The diff itself does not demonstrate failing behavior due to missing tests, nor is there an established requirement in the diff that tests must be added. So this is a valid suggestion but not a ‘real problem’ in the strict sense requested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts catch block discards the error and uses console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails") instead of the project logger, making email failures undiagnosable in production

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` block swallows the exception and logs only a generic string, not the actual `err` (message/stack) and not via any structured/project logger. This makes it difficult to diagnose why email sending failed in production and the error is effectively discarded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:41-42 builds `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` which is always truthy, making the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback dead code and showing users raw text like 'FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission'

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` handler does `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template literal always returns a string; even when `err.data?.code` is `undefined` it becomes the truthy string `"undefined: ..."`. That makes the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback effectively dead, and it will display raw/internal values like `FORBIDDEN` and message keys such as `you_do_not_have_permission` (or `undefined: ...`) to users instead of a generic localized error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:66 onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog} bypasses the Cancel button's reset, so dismissing via Escape/overlay/X leaves multiEmailValue and isInvalidEmail populated and reopening shows stale emails and a stale error banner

adjudication.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog, local state is only reset in two places: onSuccess (setMultiEmailValue([""]) and setIsOpenDialog(false)) and the Cancel button handler (setMultiEmailValue([""]), setIsInvalidEmail(false), setIsOpenDialog(false)). However the Dialog is wired as `<Dialog open={isOpenDialog} onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}>`, so closing the dialog via Escape, overlay click, or the dialog “X” (any mechanism that triggers onOpenChange) will only toggle `isOpenDialog` and will NOT clear `multiEmailValue` or `isInvalidEmail`. Reopening the dialog will therefore show the previous emails and/or the previous validation error banner. This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:26 uses key={index} on a list that supports removal, so deleting a middle entry re-associates DOM/input state (focus, uncontrolled internals, validation) with the wrong row

adjudication.rationale: In packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx the list is rendered with `value.map((field, index) => <li key={index}>...)` and items can be removed via `updatedValue.splice(index, 1)`. When a middle entry is deleted, subsequent rows shift indices, so their `key` values change. React will then reuse/move the existing EmailField components/DOM nodes for different emails, which can cause UI state (focus, cursor position, any internal EmailField state/validation) to be associated with the wrong row. This is a known correctness/UX issue with index keys in mutable lists and is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:2 imports Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip from the @calcom/ui barrel while packages/ui/index.tsx exports the component via MultiEmailLazy, creating a barrel cycle that can yield undefined components depending on module resolution order

packages/ui/form/MultiEmailLazy.tsx:3 comment '/** These are like 40kb that not every user needs */' is copy-pasted from PhoneInputLazy/AddressInputLazy and is false — MultiEmail is a ~90-line component with no heavy dependency, so the stated lazy-loading rationale is wrong

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a copied comment in `MultiEmailLazy.tsx` stating the component is “like 40kb”, but this is not a verifiable bug/security/correctness issue in the code itself—it's at most a potentially inaccurate/misleading comment. Also, the actual bundle size cannot be confirmed from the diff alone (dependencies/compiled output aren’t shown). This falls under a documentation/style nit rather than a clear defect introduced by the change.
